card.name: Present-tense verb after a subject
card.fires_on: Present-tense auxiliary or main verbs such as has, will, is, or display, right after a noun subject or relative word. Often the verb is has before been or learned.

modes.label: has before a participle
modes.description: The verb has after a subject or 'that/which', leading into a past participle like been or learned.
modes.example: Banks claim ownership of the cash that<< has>> been deposited by their customers.

modes.label: other present-tense verbs
modes.description: Verbs like will, is, display or misses placed directly after a subject, sometimes after an adverb.
modes.example: They can predict where the tidal wave<< will>> peak, and where it will be most

card.writes: It suppresses time-adverb continuations like now and stayed and promotes recently, last and originally, which suggests it steers away from adverbs that follow the verb.
card.plain: It fires on the verb right after a subject, mostly 'has' in 'has been', in ordinary prose.
